{{Short description|Polish political activist (1941–2024)}}
[[File:Wujec Ludwika.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Wujec in 2024]]
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2024}}
'''Ludwika Wujec''' (2 April 1941 – 26 May 2024) was a Polish physicist, teacher, politician, and political activist. Wujec was a member of the pro-democracy [[Dissident movement in the People's Republic of Poland|dissident movement]] against the [[Polish People's Republic]] during the country's communist era.<ref name=pn>{{cite news |first= |last=|title=Nie żyje Ludwika Wujec. Miała 83 lata |url=https://www.polsatnews.pl/wiadomosc/2024-05-26/nie-zyje-ludwika-wujec-miala-83-lata/ |work=[[Polsat News]] |publisher= |date=26 May 2024 |access-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526131539/https://www.polsatnews.pl/wiadomosc/2024-05-26/nie-zyje-ludwika-wujec-miala-83-lata/ |archive-date=26 May 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Biography==
Wujec was born on 2 April 1941, to Jewish parents Oskar and Regina (Burgierman) Okrent, in [[Soviet annexation of Eastern Galicia and Volhynia|Soviet-annexed]] [[Lviv]], in present-day [[Ukraine]].<ref name=pn/> Her parents were [[tailors]].<ref name=pn/> [[Nazi Germany]] seized Lviv during [[Operation Barbarossa]] in June 1941, just months after her birth. Wujec spent the first years of her life living in the [[Soviet Union]] with her mother as a [[refugee]] near [[Stalingrad]] and the [[Ural Mountains]] region.<ref name=pn/> Her father, Oskara, fought in the [[Second Polish Army (1944-45)|Second Polish Army]], a [[Polish People's Army]] unit formed in the Soviet Union, and was killed at the Battle of Dresden in 1945.<ref name=pn/>

Wujec returned to Poland with her mother in 1946 after [[World War II]].<ref name=pn/> She graduated from Juliusza Słowackiego High School in [[Warsaw]] received her degree from the Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry at the [[University of Łódź]].<ref name=pn/> She initially joined the ruling communist [[Polish United Workers' Party]] and became a math and physics teacher during the 1950s and 1960s.<ref name=pn/> In 1970, she married [[Henryk Wujec]], a Polish physicist, politician and social activist. The couple remained together until his death in 2020.<ref name=pn/>

In 1980, Henryk Wujec joined the [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]] trade union. One year later, Ludwika Wujec joined Solidarity's press and media agency. Wujec was arrested and imprisoned for her affiliation with Solidarity during the period of [[Martial law in Poland]], which lasted from 1981 to 1983.<ref name=pn/>
 
Wujec became an assistant to [[Tadeusz Mazowiecki]], a prominent Solidarity leader and first post-communist prime minister, during the late 1980s, including during the [[Polish Round Table Agreement]] negotiations in 1989.<ref name=pn/> She then served as the deputy director of [[Lech Wałęsa]]'s Office of the Citizen Committee.<ref name=pn/>
 
Following the fall of Communism, Wujec entered Warsaw city government. She served as the secretary and governing board member for the now-defunct {{ill|Warszawa-Centrum commune|pl|Warszawa-Centrum (commune)}} from 1995 until 2002.<ref name=pn/> In 1998, Wujec was elected to the [[Warsaw County (1999–2002)|Warsaw County]], which was disestablished in 2002. She retired from elected politics in 2002.<ref name=pn/>

Wujec died on 26 May 2024, at the age of 83. Her death was announced by her son, Paweł Wujec.<ref name=pn/> She was buried with her late husbamd, Henryk Wujec, in [[Powązki Military Cemetery]] in Warsaw on 29 May 2024.<ref name=wprost>{{cite news |first= |last=|title=Ostatnie pożegnanie Ludwiki Wujec. Syn zmarłej miał prośbę do żałobników |url=https://www.wprost.pl/kraj/11705590/pogrzeb-ludwiki-wujec-opozycjonistka-z-czasow-prl-spoczela-na-powazkach-wojskowych.html |work=[[Wprost]] |publisher= |date=29 May 2024 |access-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529161905/https://www.wprost.pl/kraj/11705590/pogrzeb-ludwiki-wujec-opozycjonistka-z-czasow-prl-spoczela-na-powazkach-wojskowych.html |archive-date=29 May 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Awards and decorations==
[[File:Kobiety Wolności 23 (cropped - Ludwika Wujec).jpg|thumb|right|250px|Wujec as depicted in the ''Kobiety Wolności'' mural at the [[Gdańsk Strzyża railway station]].]]
[[President of Poland|President]] [[Lech Kaczyński]] awarded her the Officer's Cross of the [[Order of Polonia Restituta]] in 2006.<ref name=mp2006>{{cite news |first= |last=|title=M.P. 2006 nr 62 poz. 647: Postanowienie Prezydenta Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej z dnia 14 czerwca 2006 r. o nadaniu orderów i odznaczeń |url=https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WMP20060620647/O/M20060647.pdf |work=Office of the [[President of Poland]] |publisher=[[Internetowy System Aktów Prawnych]] |date=14 June 2006 |access-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327075817/https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WMP20060620647/O/M20060647.pdf |archive-date=27 March 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2015, President [[Bronisław Komorowski]] further awarded Wujec the [[Cross of Freedom and Solidarity]].<ref name=isap>{{cite news |first= |last=|title=M.P. 2015 poz. 886: Postanowienie Prezydenta Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej z dnia 23 lipca 2015 r. o nadaniu odznaczeń. |url=https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WMP20150000886/O/M20150886.pdf |work=Office of the [[President of Poland]] |publisher=[[Internetowy System Aktów Prawnych]] |date=14 September 2015 |access-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200617034448/http://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WMP20150000886/O/M20150886.pdf |archive-date=17 June 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> Wujec and her husband, Henryk Wujec, were jointly awarded the {{ill|Professor Zbigniew Hołda Award|pl|Stowarzyszenie im. Prof. Zbigniewa Hołdy}} in 2016.<ref name=zh>{{cite news |first= |last=|title=Awards Winners |url=https://stowarzyszenieholda.pl/projekty/nagroda-im-prof-zbigniewa-holdy/laureaci-nagrody/ |work=Professor Zbigniew Hołda Association |publisher= |date= |access-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529174036/https://stowarzyszenieholda.pl/projekty/nagroda-im-prof-zbigniewa-holdy/laureaci-nagrody/ |archive-date=29 May 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2019, Wujec's image was included on the new "Women of Freedom" (''[[Kobiety Wolności]]'') [[mural]] at the [[Gdańsk Strzyża railway station]] in [[Gdańsk]], which honors women involved with the anti-Communist [[Dissident movement in the People's Republic of Poland|dissident movement]].<ref name=gd>{{cite news |first=Izabela |last=Biała |title=Kobiety Wolności - niezwykły mural na stacji PKM Strzyża przypomina polskie opozycjonistki |url=https://www.gdansk.pl/wiadomosci/kobiety-wolnosci-niezwykly-mural-na-stacji-pkm-strzyza-przypomina-polskie-opozycjonistki%2Ca%2C150093 |work= gdańsk.pl |publisher= |date=5 July 2019 |access-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202231532/https://www.gdansk.pl/wiadomosci/kobiety-wolnosci-niezwykly-mural-na-stacji-pkm-strzyza-przypomina-polskie-opozycjonistki,a,150093 |archive-date=2 December 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Other Polish female activists honored with Wujec in the mural include [[Anna Walentynowicz]] and [[Henryka Krzywonos]].<ref name=gd/>
